name: Highlands 39

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, where a curved driveway departs from the public road and winds through open desert scrub terrain to reach the residence|The main structure is a multi-wing single-story home with a dark hip roof, and a detached structure with a similar roof profile is visible to the right of the main residence|The front approach is open with low desert vegetation and scattered juniper trees providing partial screening on either side of the driveway|A small area of green lawn is visible on the left side of the residence near the front.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the broad open desert terrain to the east and the public road running along the far right edge of the frame|The residence and detached structure are visible in the right-center of the view, surrounded by low scrub and scattered juniper trees|A cleared sandy area consistent with a parking or staging surface is visible immediately adjacent to the structures on this side|No fencing, walls, or access obstructions are visible along the right side of the property.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where the residence sits on relatively flat open terrain with no rear fencing or enclosures visible|Scattered juniper trees are distributed across the rear yard area, and a cleared rectangular lawn area is visible directly behind the main structure|The rear of the property transitions directly into open undeveloped desert land with no defined boundary features|Responder access to the rear is unobstructed by fencing or walls, though desert scrub and trees reduce direct sightlines to the back of the structure.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the public road visible at the far left edge and the driveway connection point to the road clearly visible|The multi-wing residence occupies the center-right of the view, with the detached structure adjacent to it and a sandy cleared area between and around the structures|Scattered juniper trees are present along the left side of the property between the road and the structures|No fencing, gates, or access barriers are visible along the left side of the property.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single curved driveway departing from a public road to the northwest, with a long approach of approximately 200 to 300 feet through open desert terrain. The surrounding land is flat to gently sloping open desert with low scrub and scattered juniper trees, providing clear sightlines to the structure from the approach road. No fencing, gates, or vehicle barriers are visible anywhere on the property perimeter, allowing unrestricted perimeter access on all sides. A cleared sandy area adjacent to the main structure and detached building provides potential staging space for emergency vehicles.
clarifications: Does the driveway surface support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus such as fire engines or ladder trucks? Is the detached structure used as a garage, workshop, or other occupied space, and does it have its own entry doors? Are there any locked gates or access controls along the driveway that are not visible in the imagery? Is there a secondary emergency access point to the property from the road to the east or southeast? Are any utilities such as propane tanks or electrical service equipment located on the exterior of the structures that are not visible from above?
